title: Write a Pod Manifest From Scratch
intro: Everything so far has been imperative one-liners. Real manifests — and the CKA exam — need you to write YAML by hand. This lab writes a blank file for you to fill in with your own editor, then checks the actual structure once you apply it.

steps.prompt: Create a Pod named 'db' running the postgres:15 image, exposing container port 5432, with a memory limit of 512Mi and a memory request of 256Mi.
steps.hint: Skeleton: apiVersion: v1 / kind: Pod / metadata.name / spec.containers is a list of one item with name, image, ports (a list of {containerPort: ...}), and resources.limits / resources.requests, each with a memory key.
steps.solution:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  containers:
  - name: db
    image: postgres:15
    ports:
    - containerPort: 5432
    resources:
      limits:
        memory: 512Mi
      requests:
        memory: 256Mi
steps.explanation: This is exactly the kind of manifest 'kubectl run' can't produce on its own — resource limits and requests aren't available as kubectl run flags, so hand-writing YAML (or using --dry-run=client -o yaml as a starting point) is the only way to set them.
steps.why: In a real exam or incident, you'd often start from 'kubectl run db --image=postgres:15 --dry-run=client -o yaml > pod.yaml' to get the skeleton right, then hand-edit in the parts kubectl run can't express — that's faster and less error-prone than typing the whole thing from memory.
